question: Should Claw apply support inline MCP server config writes now, and if so what consent or trust UX must guard that persistent config mutation?
rationale: The PR adds a new manifest-driven path that can save MCP commands, URLs, and headers into user config, which is a config and security-sensitive product boundary rather than a purely mechanical installer change.

options.title: Allow With Explicit Apply Consent
options.body: Keep the existing MCP config writer path, but update the Claw apply confirmation/json wording and tests so users are told `--yes` can persist MCP server config.

options.title: Require Dedicated MCP Acknowledgement
options.body: Add a separate flag or prompt for inline MCP server artifacts before they can write `mcp.servers` entries from a Claw manifest.

options.title: Pause With The Stack
options.body: Keep this draft paused until the Claws RFC and prerequisite artifact PR settle the broader apply and trust policy.

recommendation.title: Allow With Explicit Apply Consent
recommendation.body: Keep the existing MCP config writer path, but update the Claw apply confirmation/json wording and tests so users are told `--yes` can persist MCP server config.

likelyOwner.reason: The current reusable MCP config writer and normalization path are attributed to this recent history, making this the best available owner for the config contract question.
